target_customer: Professionals and small teams who make many phone calls and want searchable notes and transcripts; sold by monthly calling plans.
problem: People on phone calls cannot listen and take notes at once, and details and action items get lost or are not shared with teammates.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscription with monthly calling minutes plans (about 9 to 99 dollars a month after a 60 minute free trial)
product_category: AI phone call transcription and note taking app

founders.name: Jon Goldsmith
founders.background_notes: Described as setting out to prove deep learning can fix voice transcription (TechCrunch seed coverage).

founders.name: Nikolas Liolios
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page and Crunchbase.

competitors.name: TapeACall
competitors.what: iPhone call recorder that merges the call into a three way recording line
competitors.traction_then: App store listing claims millions of users (undated listing)

competitors.name: Applicalls
competitors.what: Android app that records calls and turns them into searchable text

competitors.name: Yack.net
competitors.what: Team product with auto transcribed calls, messaging, video and files

competitors.what: Automatic recording and transcription of calls

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a VoIP dialer with Twilio, speech recognition and a note layer was standard engineering with a hard part in transcription accuracy; reviewers said notes were rough at launch.

defensibility.rationale: Speech recognition came from commodity components and several call recording apps already existed, so copying was fast. A dedicated number gave mild switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zoom added automatic transcription by early 2018; no source shows incumbents buying the company, and the exit details are not public.

market_need_then: Call recording apps such as TapeACall already had millions of downloads, and VentureBeat in February 2018 described a crowded set of transcription and note taking products, which shows demand but also a crowded field.

branding.domain_note: Product site was asktetra.com; the domain now hosts an unrelated betting promotion.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and functional: 'focus, remember the details, keep your team in sync'.

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launches in Nov 2017 with positive comments on dialer UX and requests for Android; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many other companies (for example TetraScience), no brand assets found, and the app had a small team of five at the 2018 update.

outcome_analysis: Tetra launched its iOS app in late 2017 after raising a 1.5 million dollar seed led by Amplify Partners and added inbound call support in February 2018 with a team of five. The YC directory lists it as acquired, but no announcement naming the buyer, price or date was found, so it is not clear whether this was a product exit or a soft landing for the team. A Dealroom page that names Atrium in January 2018 is an unverified, AI labelled summary and is not relied on.
notes: Funding cross checked between VentureBeat (Feb 2018, 1.5 million seed) and TechCrunch and CB Insights snippets (Amplify lead, Aug 2017). CB Insights also lists an earlier undated amount seed entry in March 2017 and total of 1.62 million; not recorded. Another CB Insights Tetra profile with 10.5 million in December 2023 is a different company. Atrium acquisition claim from Dealroom is unverified and conflicting; CB Insights comparison mentioning Dubber appears to concern Notiv. Company website asktetra.com is no longer Tetra's site. TapeACall traction figure comes from a current app store listing, not 2017.
